assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory predicted flat bands at a small twist angle and experiment then found correlated-insulator and superconducting states in magic-angle graphene. This created a tunable platform for strongly correlated electrons and is a rare theory-then-experiment sequence with a field-wide impact on moire quantum matter.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum-model prediction and the Jarillo-Herrero group experiments are the decisive pair. Rafi Bistritzer is a co-author of the theory paper, and a two-person prize naming MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero is the cleanest configuration but would leave Bistritzer out. Others, for example the Cao-related experimental authors and the fabrication contributors, also have claims.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by many groups since 2018 and extended to twisted multilayers, TMDs and fractional Chern insulators. The field is still moving fast, but the core discovery is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: The origin of superconductivity in the magic-angle system is not settled.
How to weigh the early theory contributions of Bistritzer against MacDonald is uncertain from the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Vicsek model, the Toner-Tu hydrodynamic theory and the Ramaswamy active-matter work established that driven self-propelled units escape equilibrium constraints, for example long-range order in two dimensions. It is a general statistical-physics framework for collective motion, with a broad reach into biology and soft matter. It is close to my own area, so I weigh it carefully, but its conceptual originality is high.
assessment.attribution: Vicsek (numerical model), Toner and collaborators (hydrodynamic theory and the flocking phase) and Ramaswamy (active hydrodynamics and stress) form a natural three-person group. Tu and other co-developers of the theory are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Quantitative confirmation in experiments on bacteria, colloidal rollers and vibrated granular matter exists, but a clean experimental test of the Toner-Tu exponents is limited. The theory is mature while the experimental case is still partial.
uncertainties: Strength of direct experimental verification of the predicted scaling exponents.
Other founding contributors, such as Toner's collaborators, are not in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold atoms in optical lattices realize Hubbard-type many-body models with tunable parameters, for example the superfluid to Mott-insulator transition, and allow site-resolved microscopy. This turned quantum simulation into an experimental method for strongly correlated matter and has had a lasting effect on many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch and colleagues) proposed the Hubbard-model realization, and Bloch and Greiner carried out the Mott transition and the quantum-gas microscope. Esslinger is a strong alternative to Greiner for the fermionic work. The three named here give a coherent theory-plus-experiment configuration, but the field has several deserving leaders.
assessment.maturity: Replicated across many groups and continents, and the platform now supports quantum-gas microscopes and fermionic Hubbard studies. The recognition is mature, and the older prize for Bose-Einstein condensation does not overlap with the lattice simulation.
uncertainties: Hubbard-model proposals involved Jaksch, Gardiner and others who are not in the credit list.
Whether Esslinger should take the place of Greiner.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock with a magic wavelength and the ensuing stability near the 1e-18 level changed precision metrology and opened tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. The concept is original and the practical effect is large.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice-clock concept and Ye drove its record performance, so the two-person configuration is clean and well supported. Hall and Hansch received the 2005 prize for the comb, and the clock is distinct.
assessment.maturity: Several independent laboratories reproduce clocks at the 1e-18 level and the international redefinition process is progressing. This is timely and mature.
uncertainties: Others, for example Hall and Hansch from the frequency-comb side and ion-clock groups, partially overlap in the broad area of optical clocks.
The extent to which the redefinition of the second counts for impact is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators extended topological band theory beyond the quantum Hall case, and the HgTe experiment confirmed the edge states. This is a concept with a broad effect on materials discovery and on later topological physics. It is partly adjacent to the 2016 topological-phase prize, so novelty is the main concern.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the theory of the Z2 classification, and Molenkamp led the HgTe experiment. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe route, and Fu, Kane and Moore, and Hasan and Moore contributions on 3D insulators are not in this set. This leaves a real attribution problem.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in HgTe, in Bi-based 3D materials with ARPES and in several later platforms. The topic is mature but practical applications have been slow.
uncertainties: Competing credit for the HgTe prediction and the 3D topological-insulator discovery.
Closeness to the 2016 topological-phase recognition may reduce priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KPZ equation gave a minimal nonlinear stochastic model of kinetic roughening and a universality class that connects growth, directed polymers, random matrices and integrable probability. Exact solutions linked it to Tracy-Widom statistics, and it has been observed in turbulent liquid-crystal experiments. This is a very strong conceptual contribution to nonequilibrium statistical physics, which I know well.
assessment.attribution: The original KPZ paper is by Kardar, Parisi and Zhang. The supplied credit has Spohn instead of Parisi, and Spohn's contribution is mathematical and came later. I would propose Kardar and Zhang, and I recognize that excluding Parisi is a concern since he was an original author, but Parisi is not in the credited names and he already received the 2021 prize.
assessment.maturity: Exact results came around 2010 and experimental verification by Takeuchi and Sano in 2010-2011, so the case is mature, although clean confirmation in other growth systems is still debated.
uncertainties: The omission of Parisi from the supplied names raises an allocation issue.
The experimental evidence is concentrated in a few systems.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The BB84 protocol and Ekert's entanglement-based version established information-theoretic secure key distribution from quantum principles, and the field has become an experimental and commercial area. The idea is original and clear, and its link to foundations is strong.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard authored BB84, the earliest and most clearly decisive work. Ekert's 1991 protocol is independent and also credited, so a three-person prize is possible, but I would give priority to the two-person origin. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea complicates priority and Wiesner is not on the list.
assessment.maturity: Many demonstrations, satellite links and fiber networks exist, but security in real devices and practical deployment are still developing. The 2022 prize recognized Bell-test experiments that relate to the foundations, so overlap is partial.
uncertainties: Wiesner's earlier idea and the priority question.
Practical security and impact of deployed systems remain debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming picture unifies rigidity of glasses, foams, grains and colloids around a critical point with scaling and isostaticity, and it links to marginal stability and to ideas used for high-dimensional landscapes. It is conceptually attractive for complex systems and has stimulated a lot of theory and simulation.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel proposed the jamming phase diagram, and Wyart developed the isostatic and marginal-stability theory. The supplied three-person group is coherent, but I would give priority to the founders. The reasoning for omitting Wyart is weaker than for the others.
assessment.maturity: The scaling at the transition is supported by simulations and some experiments, but the connection to real glasses and the role of dimension are still debated, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: The relevance of the idealized jamming point to real laboratory materials.
Weighing Wyart's contribution against the founders.
